summary: Multiple Lenis instances created: useLenis() called in SceneProgressIndicator and again in Home component, creating two independent smooth-scroll controllers that conflict
failure_scenario: Two Lenis instances attach separate scroll listeners and RAF loops, fighting for control of window.scrollTo. Causes scroll jank, stuttering, or complete scroll breakdown during navigation.

summary: Multiple Lenis instances created: useLenis() called in Home component and also in SceneProgressIndicator, creating two independent smooth-scroll controllers that conflict
failure_scenario: Two Lenis instances attach separate scroll listeners and RAF loops, fighting for control of window.scrollTo. Causes scroll jank, stuttering, or complete scroll breakdown during navigation.

summary: Stale closure in playSequence: setTimeout callbacks capture playAmbientTone with stale isMuted value, causing sounds to play after mute is enabled
failure_scenario: User calls playSequence while unmuted, then toggles mute on. Pending setTimeout callbacks still reference old playAmbientTone with isMuted=false in closure, playing sounds despite mute being active.

summary: AudioContext not reinitialized after close: cleanup closes AudioContext but doesn't reset initializedRef, causing silent sound failure on remount
failure_scenario: Component mounts → AudioContext created → unmounts → AudioContext closed but initializedRef stays true → remount skips initialization → all sound functions fail silently because audioContextRef.current is closed.

summary: SceneProvider context value recreated every scroll frame: useMemo depends on progress (updated 60fps), causing all 6 scene components to re-render every frame during active scene
failure_scenario: User scrolls → progress updates 60fps → SceneProvider creates new context object → all 6 scene components (OpeningScene, HeroScene, GenesisScene, OracleScene, AfterimageScene, FinaleScene) re-render 60fps → catastrophic performance with complex Three.js scenes.

summary: CustomCursor re-renders 60fps: subscribes to entire cursor store (x, y change every frame), no React.memo, creating new style objects every frame
failure_scenario: Mouse moves → cursor store x/y update 60fps → CustomCursor re-renders 60fps → new style objects created → React reconciliation overhead → frame drops on lower-end devices.

summary: useSceneSound creates orphaned timeouts: setInterval calls playSequence which creates setTimeouts, but cleanup only clears interval, leaving pending timeouts to fire after unmount/scene change
failure_scenario: Scene changes rapidly → old interval cleared but playSequence timeouts from previous scene still fire → sounds play for inactive scenes → audio context errors if unmounted.

summary: Dynamic require() used instead of import: const { SCENES } = require('@/types') inside hook function defeats static analysis, tree-shaking, and executes on every hook call
failure_scenario: Every useLenis() call executes require() at runtime instead of compile-time import. Defeats bundler optimizations, may cause issues with webpack alias resolution, and runs on every hook invocation.

summary: Magnetic elements memory leak: addMagneticElement cleanup only runs on component unmount, not when element removed from DOM via conditional rendering; removeMagneticElement doesn't remove event listeners
failure_scenario: Element conditionally rendered ({show && <div ref={el} />}) → show becomes false → element removed from DOM but cleanup not called → element stays in magneticElementsRef Map indefinitely → memory leak. removeMagneticElement only deletes from Map, leaves dangling mousemove/mouseleave listeners.

summary: useState import placed after component definitions: import { useState } from 'react' at line 245 but used in SoundToggle (line 72) and SceneProgressIndicator (line 123) defined earlier
failure_scenario: While ES module hoisting makes this work at runtime, it violates conventions, confuses developers, and triggers ESLint errors (no-use-before-define, import/order).

summary: SceneContext defined after SceneProvider that uses it: const SceneContext = createContext() at line 123 but SceneProvider uses SceneContext.Provider at line 117; React import at bottom (line 138)
failure_scenario: While currently works due to ES module evaluation order (context initialized before render), this is a code smell that risks TDZ errors if module-level JSX usage is added. Import at bottom is confusing and non-standard.

summary: Duplicate preconnect to fonts.gstatic.com: two identical <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" /> tags wasted preconnect slot
failure_scenario: Browser preconnect limit (~6-8 per origin) consumed by duplicate. Fixed - duplicate removed.
